One week in Maine. One shot a day.  I’ve seen this done before and loved the idea.  It really challenges you to constantly be thinking as you go about your day and always looking for a great shot or angle. More importantly, it forced me to slow down. Take in every scenery. Spend little extra time at every destination, whether it was a pull off on the side of the road in Acadia National Park or stay seated on a rock somewhere watching nature pass.  Enjoying the moment is the reason why we out there so make sure you stay a little longer.  #nature #peace #maine #naturephotography #cinematic

RANDOM DART EDIT - PART 1 🌎🌍🌏 One dart. One random destination. One little film. I threw a dart at a map of the world, booked a trip to wherever it landed, and turned the experience into a cinemaitc video edit. For those who haven’t followed along from the beginning: I started this experiment with a map of Vienna, then moved on to Austria, Europe, and finally the entire world. With every episode, the challenge staya the same: take a random location and turn it into a short visual portrait of that place. This is my attempt to translate an entire destination into a tiny piece of video art. 🎥 I genuinely love making this series, and I hope you enjoy watching it, follow for part 2! #canada #travel #filmmaking

In 2013, two American rappers named Pacman and Peso travelled to North Korea to film a music video for their song Escape to North Korea. They raised over $10,000 through a Kickstarter campaign to finance the unusual trip. During their five-day stay, they filmed various locations in the country, including the streets of Pyongyang, the subway, famous monuments and even a rice farm. Since North Korea is one of the most isolated countries in the world and has strict rules regarding filming and media, the project was very unusual. The video was released in January 2014 and attracted attention because it showed a rare perspective of North Korea through the eyes of two American rappers. The world is looking at Shenzhen. But how much do you really know about this city? Give me eight minutes, and let me show you China's City of the Future — my home city, Shenzhen! After three months of planning, filming and production, I'm excited to share the latest episode of Explore China's Nature and Culture: Shenzhen. From ancient history to China's reform and opening-up, from manufacturing to innovation, and from the people who built this city to the mountains, coastline and wildlife we share it with — this documentary explores the stories behind Shenzhen's extraordinary transformation. As Shenzhen takes centre stage for APEC 2026, I hope this film helps you discover not just its skyscrapers and technological achievements, but also the people, culture and everyday life that make this city so special. All historical footage featured in this documentary is authentic and used with permission. No AI-generated footage has been used. Welcome to my city. Welcome to Shenzhen!  #Shenzhen #China #APEC2026 #ExploreChina #Shenzhenchina #ChinaTravel #Documentary
